name: Colin Walsh

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am with the Work Futures Panel, independent of employers, AI companies, unions and government. Your answers are confidential. What is a normal day at work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 43 and still a junior accountant, though I have a bachelor’s degree in accounting. I enter invoices and start tax returns, then a senior catches codes I still get wrong. I use our approved AI sorter every day, but I check its suggestions against receipts and talk through mistakes at the paid weekly junior huddle. I enjoy showing a new starter why a receipt matters, but hurried files with missing papers wear me out.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: How does the rest of your day work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: Eva, my partner, works at a pharmacy and we trade school pickup for our two children. Our mortgage is covered by two wages, my junior pay is unusually good, and we have about ten months of expenses saved. There are plenty of accounting firms nearby, and I usually speak up for paid training and a fair voice for staff.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team a small shortcut is useful if it buys time to ask clients for missing papers. We still need a named accountant to check the return before filing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our mortgage is manageable on my above-average junior pay and my partner’s wage, and we have roughly ten months of expenses saved. A little automation does not threaten the household, though I worry about juniors losing practice.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would keep using the approved AI tool I use each day to sort invoices, then compare its flags with paper receipts. In the first year I would keep preparing returns and bring one error example to the weekly junior huddle so the new starters can learn it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about my own pay and work. I would feel cross if a few saved minutes became a reason to stop teaching people.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What was the error this week?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The tool put a parent’s school trip payment among a client’s shop costs because the card was the same. I found the receipt and showed the new starter why the account was wrong.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who pays for the huddle time?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our firm already pays for a weekly half-hour review with the senior accountant, so I would use that slot. I would not ask the juniors to stay late for a training talk.

say: I would use small **time savings** to chase missing client papers.
I would keep **named sign-off** on every return.
think: Our **ten-month cushion** and two wages make my income secure here.
I worry about losing **junior practice** even if my hours stay whole.
do: Keep using the **approved invoice tool** and checking flags against receipts.
Prepare returns and share one **error example** in the paid weekly junior huddle.
feel: I feel **calm** about our pay and cross about any lost learning time.
S0.quote: I would not ask the juniors to stay late for a training talk.
fieldNote: His **daily AI use** is grounded in receipt checks and an error he showed a new starter.
The **paid huddle** matters to him: he wants training inside ordinary hours, with the household financially secure in this mild scenario.

steps.text: Keep preparing returns with approved invoice tool and source-receipt checks
Share one error example in existing paid weekly junior huddle

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say the firm should show staff the hours saved and how those hours are shared. If junior entry work goes, we need paid time to learn the checks that remain.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My invoice sorting and first tax drafts could shrink because they are exactly the thinking tasks software can do. We have ten months saved and plenty of firms nearby, so I am concerned about the trade but not expecting a missed mortgage payment soon.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would ask our staff association to collect junior hours and unfilled-post counts, and test the approved drafting tool on six old returns during the paid huddle. In the first year, if my hours are cut, I would apply for an advertised local junior tax post with written salary and hours at least equal to my current job; I would stay on payroll until an offer and start date are confirmed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about my paid hours, though I am not frantic about family bills. The records would help us ask for paid learning rather than guess.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell the association to ask for?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for a report on lost junior hours and a paid training slot for each remaining reviewer. Our group can ask the partners together without putting client names in the report.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if a local firm offers less?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the current paid hours while they last and decline a lower wage unless our savings are running down. A new title does not pay the mortgage by itself.

say: I would ask the firm to **publish hours saved** and protect paid junior learning.
I would take **staff figures** to the partners together.
think: My **first drafts** may shrink as software takes thinking work.
Ten months saved and **many local firms** reduce near-term household danger.
do: Collect **junior-hour figures** through the staff association.
Test **six old returns** in the approved drafting tool during paid review time.
Seek **posted local jobs** after cuts, retaining shifts until confirmed start; require written equal pay/hours unless savings dwindle.
feel: I feel **anxious** about my own hours, while our mortgage remains covered.
S1.quote: A new title does not pay the mortgage by itself.
fieldNote: His **collective request** is concrete: junior hours, vacancies and paid learning time, without client identifiers.
The **ten-month reserve** lets him reject lower pay and search while keeping existing shifts until a real start date.

steps.text: Collect junior hours and vacancy counts through staff association
Test approved drafting tool on six old returns during paid huddle
Apply for advertised local post with written equal pay/hours after cuts; retain shifts until start date
Consider lower pay only if household savings run down

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the staff that AGI by 2028 reaches our tax screens in 2028; capable robots around 2031 do not grant office work more time. The firm owes juniors a clear staffing forecast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect most junior drafting hours, including mine, to disappear when cheaper AGI can do the thinking. Ten months of savings gives us time, but replacing this unusually good junior wage across many firms could be harder than finding a listing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would ask the staff association to seek written notice of planned hour cuts and employer-paid training in client tax queries. If the firm approves fees and paid study hours in writing, I would enrol before 2028; in the first year after AGI arrives, if my hours fall, I would take a vacant paid query post only with written salary and hours at least equal to my current job, or apply to advertised local firms while keeping any paid shifts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about losing a well-paid job, but I can picture a search rather than a crisis. Our ten-month savings were built for a change like AGI by 2028.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the firm refuses to fund the course?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would practise client questions on old files with my senior reviewer in our paid huddle if she agrees. I would not buy a course out of the children’s reserve.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you tell your partner to take more hours?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, my partner Eva already works full-time in a pharmacy and handles school pickup twice a week. I would use our savings first, then discuss extra shifts only if an employer confirms paid hours and we can cover pickup.

say: I would say **AGI by 2028** reaches our tax screens before capable robots.
I would demand a **written staffing forecast** for junior staff.
think: I expect most of my **junior drafts** to disappear after 2028.
Our **ten-month reserve** gives time, but replacing high junior pay may be hard.
do: Seek **cut notice** through the staff association; discuss Eva’s extra shifts only if savings fall and school pickup is covered.
Enrol in **client-query training** with written fees and paid hours; otherwise practise files in paid huddle if senior agrees.
After lost hours, take a **vacant paid query post** with written equal terms or apply locally while keeping shifts.
feel: I feel **anxious** about income loss with enough savings for a search.
S2.quote: Our ten-month savings were built for a change like AGI by 2028.
fieldNote: He expects **junior work loss** at the AGI date, but a ten-month reserve and many local firms give him a plan.
He refuses to assume **Eva’s extra shifts** are available without confirmed pay and school pickup coverage; training has a free paid-huddle fallback.

steps.text: Ask staff association to seek written hour-cut notice
Enrol with written fees and paid time; otherwise practise queries in paid huddle with senior
Take vacant paid query post with written equal pay/hours after cuts or apply locally while employed
Discuss Eva’s confirmed paid shifts only if savings fall and school pickup is covered

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say AGI by 2031 gives us five years to agree on training and clear notice. Robots arriving around 2034 do not move the tax desk deadline.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years lets us keep building savings while I learn to handle client questions, but I still expect junior drafting to shrink in 2031. I would not promise the children my current wage will last forever.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would ask the senior accountant for paid time to handle two client query calls each month under her supervision, if the manager approves the hours. I would add 120 a month to savings while both wages hold; in the first year after 2031, if my draft hours are cut, I would apply for a vacant paid client-service role with written salary and hours at least equal to my current job, or keep remaining tax shifts while applying to advertised local posts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy but purposeful. A few years lets me learn from real calls and still get the children to school.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What will the senior accountant listen for?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: She will check whether I explain a missing receipt plainly and correct any tax advice before the call ends. I am still a junior and need that supervision.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the manager denies paid call time?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep preparing returns and ask to review recorded training calls during the paid huddle instead, if the client consented. I would not offer free evening work to make the plan look good.

say: I would ask for **paid supervised calls** before the 2031 change.
I would remind colleagues **2034 robots** arrive after the desk risk.
think: My **junior drafts** still face a 2031 cut.
I can add to our **family savings** while both wages continue and school pickup stays covered.
do: Learn through **two supervised client calls** monthly if the manager approves paid hours.
Save **120 monthly** while both wages hold.
After lost draft hours, seek a **vacant paid client-service role** with written equal pay and hours or apply nearby while employed.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about future pay, with time to build another skill.
S3.quote: I am still a junior and need that supervision.
fieldNote: His **supervised-call plan** fits his actual junior skill; he never assumes daily AI use makes him ready to advise alone.
If the manager denies **paid call time**, he will use consented recordings during the paid huddle instead of free evening work.

steps.text: Learn two monthly client calls if manager approves paid senior supervision
Save 120 monthly while both household wages hold
Seek vacant paid client role with written equal pay/hours after cuts or apply nearby while employed
Keep returns and review consented recordings in paid huddle if manager denies call time

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say AGI by 2036 gives families and firms a decade to build a paid path for junior accountants. The robots around 2039 do not postpone the change to our account screens.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our children will be older and the mortgage smaller if both incomes keep coming. I still expect routine junior tax drafts to go in 2036, but I could have years of supervised client work by then.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would keep preparing returns and ask to join one paid client query each month with the senior reviewer, if the manager approves it. I would pay an extra 150 monthly against the mortgage after we hold twelve months of expenses in cash, while both wages hold; in the first year after 2036, if my draft hours fall, I would take a vacant client-service job only with written pay and hours at least equal to today, or apply to advertised local posts before leaving.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about the next few years, though the end of junior drafting is real. The decade before AGI by 2036 lets me protect the children’s home without gambling the reserve.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why twelve months before extra mortgage payments?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Cash pays for a broken car or missed wage while a lower mortgage balance does not. I would keep the reserve untouched before making extra principal payments.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you start your own tax practice?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only after a year of paid client demand and a separate cash reserve for the business. I would not put the family home behind an untested idea.

say: I would ask for a **paid junior pathway** through 2036.
I would note the **2039 robots** do not protect tax desk work.
think: Older children and a smaller **mortgage** depend on both wages holding.
do: Keep **preparing returns** and learn monthly queries only with approved paid supervision.
Hold **twelve months cash**, then pay 150 monthly against principal while both wages hold.
After lost draft hours, take a **vacant client-service job** with written equal pay and hours or apply locally before leaving.
feel: I feel **calm** in the near term with a protected reserve.
S4.quote: The decade before AGI by 2036 lets me protect the children’s home without gambling the reserve.
fieldNote: His **cash-first sequence** is precise: a twelve-month reserve before extra mortgage principal payments.
He would test **paid client demand** before starting any practice, and protects the family home from an unproven business idea.

steps.text: Keep preparing returns while current paid hours continue
Learn monthly client queries only with manager-approved paid senior supervision
Hold twelve months cash then pay 150 monthly against mortgage while both wages hold
Take vacant client job with written equal pay and hours after cuts or apply locally employed

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because junior drafts could vanish before the firm agrees on paid training. Written notice, supervised client work and a real paid vacancy would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who pays for a junior to learn the mistakes software makes. A firm cannot call an unpaid evening a training plan.

headlineQuote: A firm cannot call an unpaid evening a training plan.
portrait: At **43**, Colin is a junior accountant with a bachelor’s degree, still learning tax codes while using approved AI daily.
He and **partner Eva** have two school-age children, a mortgage, high junior pay and about ten months saved.
He favours **paid training** and a staff voice, with many local firms providing real job options.
The **2028 deadline** threatens his first drafts; longer runways let him learn supervised client work and protect family savings.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could erase his junior drafts before a paid route into other work is ready.
whatWouldHelp: He wants **written notice**, supervised paid learning and a genuine vacancy with protected wages.
